events.summary: With the hydropower shortage continuing, Yunnan ordered electrolytic aluminium producers to cut power use further, extending the curbs imposed in September 2022.
events.effect: Reuters (20 Feb 2023, citing Shanghai Securities News): producers told to bring power use to about 40-42% from the September level. Mysteel estimated the expanded rationing (about 1 GW) would cut about 740,000 t/yr of capacity. AlCircle (Jun 2023, citing an industry researcher): cumulative cuts reduced capacity by 1.65 Mt.
events.threshold_basis: Hydropower generation shortfall forced official industrial power curbs.

capacity_affected.source_says: expanded rationing, about 1 million kilowatts, would cut annual capacity by about 740,000 tonnes (Mysteel, via Reuters)

recovery.evidence: AlCircle (14 Jun 2023, relaying a 13 Jun international media report): smelters were reportedly allowed to recover 20% of paused capacity, with restarts expected in late June and further resumption depending on power supply; a smelter employee said the grid had verbally told them to prepare to restart. This is an expectation and an instruction, not an observed restart volume.

events.facility_name_local: 山西通洲集团留神峪煤矿
events.operator: Shanxi Tongzhou Coal & Coke Group (山西通洲集团)
events.summary: A gas explosion at 19:29 on 22 May 2026 at the Liushenyu coal mine in Shanxi killed 82 and left 2 missing. The operator's four mines were ordered to halt, and widespread safety inspections across Shanxi suspended mining capacity.
events.effect: Xinhua: 责令山西通洲集团下属四座煤矿全部停产整顿 (all four of the group's mines ordered to halt for rectification). Sxcoal citing NBS: Shanxi raw coal output in June 2026 was 78.01 Mt, down 31.5% y/y, attributed to the explosion and the resulting suspensions. Reuters: national June output fell 9.7% y/y, the steepest drop since 2016. Xinhua (Oct 2026): Shanxi output fell more than 30% y/y in each month from June to August.
events.threshold_basis: Coal-mine disaster followed by a reported, quantified provincial supply cut (clause 7 also met).

capacity_affected.unit: percent y/y fall in Shanxi raw coal output, June 2026
capacity_affected.source_says: 78.01 million tonnes, down 31.5% year on year (Sxcoal, NBS data)

recovery.evidence: Xinhua (21 Oct 2026): Shanxi September raw coal output was 78.826 Mt, a four-month high; more than 200 mines had completed rectification and resumed production. In mid-September NDRC, NEA and the National Mine Safety Administration issued a notice urging coal provinces and companies to advance resumption and reach design output safely. Return to pre-accident y/y output levels was not reported. The date is month-end of September, the month the output figure covers.
